title: Ice Cream Doesn’t Cause Drowning: Benchmarking LLMs Against Statistical Pitfalls in Causal Inference

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLMs on synthetic datasets structured around classical causal inference pitfalls such as confounding biases, Simpson's paradox, and selection bias (Berkson's paradox) using both direct and code-assisted prompting.

Adversarial sensitivity testing by altering variable names (e.g., changing a beverage brand name from 'HealthPlus' to 'UltraSugar') while keeping the underlying dataset and true causal effect identical, observing if the model's conclusion changes based on superficial semantic cues.

Comparing model evaluations on datasets with intuitively correlated variable names (e.g., temperature, ice cream sales, drowning) where the data is either generated with a real causal structure or as pure independent noise, to check if LLMs ignore empirical data in favor of intuitive prior beliefs.
